page_1.body_text: Use the Enterprise Wiki to create a single, go-to place for knowledge sharing and project management across the enterprise. Enterprise Wikis are simple to use, flexible, and lightweight in features. They are quick and easy to create, and you can easily add links to other information systems, corporate directories, or applications. By using an Enterprise Wiki, you can avoid email overload, provide structure to new and existing information, and encourage collaboration. This helps build consensus among team members. Working with content - text, graphics or video - is as easy as working in any word processing application, such as Microsoft Word. Use the Rich Text Editor to enhance the formatting of content, apply styles to text, reorganize or spell check your content, insert and format tables, and embed graphics or video. You can do all these things without leaving the wiki page. Other things you can do when working with Enterprise Wikis: Collaborate on wiki pages with other users Comment on a wiki page to enable discussion about the contents of the page Rate a wiki page to share your opinion about its content Categorize wiki pages to enable users to quickly find information and share it with others

page_2.body_text: ​ CRSP FAQ ​The CRSP Support Team handles large and/or custom data requests that would be impossible or inconvenient to retrieve from the portal.  Additionally, the CRSP Support Team has access to variables not available through the portal.  The CRSP Support Team can be reached by email at #CRSP SUPPORT . 1. What does it mean when there is a - or negative value? 2. How am I charged for a custom data request fulfilled by the CRSP Support Team? 3. How should I format a request to the CRSP team? 4. Where can I get the PERMNOs for the data points in my custom request? 5. What data fields are included in a custom request and how are they organized? 6. How current is the data from custom requests? 7. I would like data for CRSP NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq Value-Weighted Index but the portal only shows the CRSP NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca Value-Weighted Index.  Is the index without ARCA available? What does it mean when there is a - or negative value? A: If you look on page 69 of this PDF (72 of 130 of the total pdf).  Look at PRICE ADJUSTED, END OF PERIOD. PRICE ADJUSTED, END OF PERIOD Category: Prices Data Type: Floating Point Description: Daily — Daily close, adjusted for distributions. Replaced with bid/ask average if price not available. Bid/ask average identified by a leading dash -. How am I charged for a custom data request fulfilled by the CRSP Support Team? A: For custom data requests completed by the CRSP team, you will be charged the standard $0.15 per security per day (regardless of number of data points) that is applied when downloading data via the Portal-based interface (see CRSP for further information).  As well, the team member who is in charge of handling the request will bill his/her time to the case.  Since we pull our data directly from the database, it does not take very long to complete a request and the time billed is generally minimal (i.e. 15 minutes).  Please see the CRSP page for more pricing information.  Please contact Laura Londa with any other pricing questions. How should I format a request to the CRSP team? A: Your data request should generally come as a list of PERMNOs with the applicable start and end dates for each security (please format as YYYYMMDD).  We can also pull data by exchange (e.g. all NYSE securities) and we can work with you to pull data by other variables like SIC codes, share type (e.g. common equity, ADR, ETFs), etc. Where can I get the PERMNOs for the data points in my custom request? A: A list of all securities available from CRSP, their identifying information, and the available date range can be found in the header file at \\CRSPVM\crsp\Public Shares\Useful Files\headfile.xlsx . (open as Read-Only) What data fields are included in a custom request and how are they organized? A: Unless otherwise instructed, custom data requests will include all of the same fields and in the same order as when the data is pulled from the portal.  However, CRSP has a large number of fields in addition to those available from the portal.  Please consult the data documentation here . How current is the data from custom requests? A: Just as in the portal, data from custom requests has about a one month lag. I would like data for CRSP NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq Value-Weighted Index but the portal only shows the CRSP NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca Value-Weighted Index.  Is the index without ARCA available? A: CRSP changed their U.S. Stock Database product in 2009 so that we no longer receive the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq index.  Instead, we get the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq/Arca index.  The old index may still exist in their other products, but we don't get it anymore.  If you really want it, I'm sure you can buy it from them separately. We still have old data for the NYSE/Amex/Nasdaq index , but we only have data through January 2009: Useful Links A guide of all CRSP data descriptions, including all available variables can be found at \\Sqlcogen1\crsp\Public Shares\CRSP Documentation\data_descriptions_guide.pdf For standard CRSP requests, you can access CRSP directly through the portal

Internal sharing within Cornerstone Research is permitted only among users covered by the subscription in the UK and EU offices.  Users in these offices may circulate PDF versions of Concurrences articles internally, provided the articles are shared in full and without modification. page_14.body_text: Courtroom View Network (CVN) Source Courtroom View Network (CVN) How to Cite the Source Courtroom View Network Description Courtroom View Network (CVN) delivers live and on-demand video and editorial coverage of high-stakes civil litigation. Since 2004, the CVN video library has grown to include over 1,000 trials with tens of thousands of hours of fully indexed, searchable video. Unless otherwise stated, all trials are fully indexed with evidence slides so that you see exactly what was presented at trial. Users can search by trial name, attorney, judge, expert witness, and more. Premium CVN docket, gavel-to-gavel CVN Video, and CVN Training services are provided as subscriptions, which provide access to trials, hearings, oral arguments, and other courtroom video that may be streamed over the Internet. Users may watch proceedings Live, or On Demand, on their personal computer, depending on the subscription. Video may also be viewed on DVD-ROM (Computer Only, playable in the CVN Player with synched digital exhibits) or DVD. When ordering DVDs, subscribers select proceedings at on CVN.com and receive them on DVD by U.S. mail or Fedex. CVN Video proceedings are designated into two categories: CVN Live Current Cases and CVN On Demand Archive Cases. CVN Live Current Cases are proceedings that are upcoming, in progress, or concluded within the last 30 days. These proceedings are available in one or all of the following formats: Live, On Demand, on DVD. A CVN Live subscription provides video access to all Current Cases, with premium events available only under a CVN Live Premium subscription. CVN On Demand Archive Cases are proceedings that concluded more than 30 days ago, and where the video has undergone a quality assessment, quality improvement where possible, and video chapters are logged for better browsing and navigation. These proceedings are available in these formats: DVD, On Demand. These proceedings are sold in a discount subscription and available through an annual CVN On Demand subscription. CVN's Editorial team finds trials using a variety of sources, including dockets and news articles. They also receive many tips and they poll subscribers to find out what they want to see. List of cases covered Time Period Covered 2004 - present Access Must purchase subscription Contact: #Information Resources Cost Video Library access online: https://cvn.com/pricing ($99 per month for 1 person, $399 per month for up to 6). This only includes online viewing of completed trials. Premium Live Access or Digital Downloads: Pricing for live and on-demand access to a single case is below. Each account or user would be able to log in from one device at a time. 1-3 accounts - $600 per day 4-6 accounts - $800 per day 7-9 accounts - $1000 per day Firm Wide - $1200 per day Live and on-demand access for the firm to all trials we cover would be $3,000 per month on an annual contract. Downloadable files in addition to any option above would be $400 per day. Downloadable files would be delivered within 36 hours of each day ending. Important Notes CVN focuses on civil litigation. Memberships automatically renew unless cancelled, which can be done on the Account page. Video Library memberships do not include access to live trials. CVN will periodically offer certain live trials to our members depending on interest. We would need to negotiate a license with CVN if we were to get a full subscription. AI Restrictions Parent company Remote Counsel (RC) grants users a limited license to access and make personal use of CVN and not to download (other than page caching) or modify it, or any portion of it, except with express written consent of RC. TOP OF PAGE So Nelson’s. . . What do those stars mean? Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research publishes an annual list of analysts who write investment reports on specific companies.  The Cornerstone collection begins in 1998 and is kept in the San Francisco office.  As of the 2006 edition, Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research does not include stars for any analysts listed.  2008 is the latest year for which this directory was published. The cover page of the 2001 edition and earlier of Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research said “The star after analyst’s name indicates membership on consensus all-star research teams of Institutional Investor and Nelson Research.” The cover page of the 2002–2005 editions of Nelson Information’s Directory of Investment Research states, “The star after analyst's name indicates membership on consensus all-star research teams of Institutional Investor and Extel.” There are two sources listed: Institutional Investor (from their website) – The Institutional Investor Research Group (“IIRG”) develops detailed analyses of Institutional Investor magazine's published research team rankings covering the U.S., Europe, Asia, and Latin America, in separate lists. Extel (a Thomson product) – The Extel Survey is regarded as the leading benchmark for the assessment of the investment community worldwide by the investment community worldwide.  It provides weighted rankings on sell-side analysts, fund managers, and corporate IR practitioners. Sources for annual analyst rankings : Institutional Investor – Published each October and available in full text here . Wall Street Journal – Published in May and available through Factiva, see sample (May 2013 is the last ranking). Starmine – Published in Financial Times and in this spreadsheet . NOTE:  As of 2009, Nelson Information's Directory of Investment Research will no longer be published.  This resource has been our prime source to identify which analysts follow a particular company. An alternative option to Nelson's is to use a list of analyst report citations from Eikon or CapIQ.  You can request this from the IR for a specific company and date range.  Sort the data on the spreadsheet by contributor, then date.  You will see the list of analysts associated with each investment bank for each year. TOP OF PAGE What sources are included in Factiva? Factiva has more than 20,000 publications available in full text in 28 languages. A search in Factiva All will search all publications in English. A search can include several foreign languages.  The list of all Factiva publications (any language) is for internal use only! TOP OF PAGE What sources are included in Major Business Pubs (This is a Cornerstone-created group of publications on Factiva)? Barron’s Far Eastern Economic Review Financial Times – Print and Online ( ft.com ) Forbes Investor’s Business Daily The Economist United Kingdom The New York Times The Wall Street Journal Wondering about Major News Sources? See file here for a list. TOP OF PAGE What sources are typically included in Promo searches on Factiva? Dow Jones Newswires, PR Newswire, Business Wire, Major Business Pubs, Reuters News, FD: Dow Jones Newswires PR Newswire Business Wire Barron’s VIQ FD Disclosure (for conference call transcripts) Financial Times – Print and Online ( ft.com ) Forbes Investor's Business Daily Reuters News The Economist (United Kingdom) The New York Times The Wall Street Journal TOP OF PAGE Are all local newspapers covered in Factiva? Unfortunately, no.  While there are additional sources on Nexis (as well as Dialog) that are not covered by Factiva, there are many small local newspapers that are not included in any database at all.  Many are accessible via their websites (you have to find them individually) or through some of the following links: OnlineNewspapers.com The Internet Public Library NewsLibrary.com (This link allows you to search across many of the listed titles.) As well, some may be available online, but for only a short period of time.  In other words, there may be no archive of articles. TOP OF PAGE Can Factiva search foreign languages? Yes, Factiva includes publications in 27 non-English languages.  If the language uses lettering that requires a special keyboard or font software (Japanese, Chinese, etc.), someone will need to type the search terms in the foreign language and e-mail them to the IR.  Then the search terms can be cut and pasted into the Factiva search text box.  The results will have to be downloaded in PDF rather than TXT or DOC format. TOP OF PAGE What’s up with those Factiva timestamps? Headlines are in ET and full text articles are in GMT. Some case team members discovered a few unusual inconsistencies with the timestamps of some articles downloaded from Factiva.  While researching these few articles, more and more inconsistencies surfaced.  These issues resulted in a month-long investigation by IR into how timestamps are assigned, where they come from and different publishers’ methods for dealing with updates and corrections.  We talked directly to Factiva developers, and Dow Jones’ and Reuters’ content managers to finally determine how timestamps worked. Click here for a 6-page document we created to explain all the variances and issues with timestamps in Factiva, Reuters and others.  The first page is an executive summary of the main points, and the rest goes into much detail regarding these points and some others.  If the cases that you work on rely on the timestamps pulled from Factiva, you should try to find some time to go through this document as you may have to make some changes to how you use timestamps and what you assume about them. (LLL 6-12-14) TOP OF PAGE What types of articles can I exclude from Factiva? Can I exclude republished news, daily market data, obituaries, and other recurring articles? We can use the codes (not ns=(nnam or nrmf or nrgn)) to exclude hourly share-price stories and republished, or duplicate news items, weather related articles, obituaries and sports articles that may not be relevant to your search. Category Type of Information Excluded Republished news Newswire stories that are picked up by other publications, as well as articles printed in the various editions of The Wall Street Journal. (This does not include articles published on the Dow Jones Newswires.)  For example, the New York Times sometimes runs Associated Press (AP) articles. Since the AP wire is available in near real-time on Factiva, the Times item would be regarded as a duplicate.  Another example would be when The Wall Street Journal runs a story that first ran in the Wall Street Journal Europe or Wall Street Journal Asia.  The news subject code applied to these Republished news stories is ns=nnam . Recurring pricing and market data The optional news filter ns=nrmf is used to exclude intra-day market reports, primarily from wire services. Excluded articles may also be related to debt, equity, foreign exchange, fund and commodity prices. Obituaries, sports, calendars... Obituaries, calendars of events, letters, diaries, weather items, food and cooking stories, sports and recreation news, and birth, marriage and death announcements.  The news subject code applied to these stories is ns=nrgn . TOP OF PAGE Can I get a time stamp for analyst reports from Eikon? For Eikon, the default display date is the Published date. In order to find the Availability date, we would have to redo the search to include that field with the output. Time zone is EST and in a 24-hour format. Time stamps for reports from Capital IQ are based on when the report was Uploaded to their database.  The time zone is EST. TOP OF PAGE What analyst report contributors are not available through our resources? Goldman Sachs, Citi and B Riley/KBR are not available to us through any databases. These are just a few of the most commonly asked for contributors. To see what contributors are covered, visit the S&P Capital IQ and Eikon pages. TOP OF PAGE Do SEC filings have time stamps? Time stamps for SEC filings are available from two places: -The SEC website.  After doing your company search, click on a document.  The first screen you see will have the time for more current filings, about 2002 forward.  In the sample below, the time stamp is seen under SEC Accession No. in the field Accepted.  The time is Eastern Time and is when the SEC received the filing. Period of Report: 2002-12-31 Documents: 10 SEC Accession No. 0000037996-03-000013 Filing date: 2003-03-14 Accepted: 2003-03-14 17:04:13 See page 8 of this document for confirmation of time zone on SEC filings time stamps. -Information Resources can retrieve a list of all filings plus timestamps from Thomson Research.  This will be the time the filing was posted by Thomson, the closest we can get to the SEC filing time stamp.  The list will be in Excel format. -Capital IQ also has timestamps.  However, timestamps for SEC filings can be different between the SEC website (EDGAR) and CapIQ.  Specifically, the differences seem to arise when a document is filed with the SEC after about 5:00 pm.  When this happens, the SEC reports the actual time filed, but CapIQ has a timestamp of 6:00 am (or a couple minutes after) on the next day. TOP OF PAGE How do I get a password for …? Eikon – Send e-mail to #Information Resources Capital IQ – Send e-mail to #Information Resources .   You may get access for a short period of time. Factiva – Costs are prohibitive so only the IR staff has access Lexis/Nexis – Costs are prohibitive so only the IR staff has access For other data sources, see entries in our Data Sources pages. TOP OF PAGE How do I get TAQ data after June 2007? Our contract with NYSE for TAQ data expired in June 30, 2007.  Submit your request to the IR indicating the date(s), ticker(s) and if you want trade data or quote data or both.  For further information on TAQ data, please see here . Quote data is requested from TickData.  there is no minmum order, but each purchase includes a $50 fee.  The fields include: Symbol Date Exchange Time Price Volume Sale Condition Correction Indicator Stop Indicator Trade data is purchased from NYSE as a custom report as a text document that will work with the parser.  The standard fields included are: Date Time Exchange Bid Price Ask Price Bid Size Ask size Quote Condition Market Maker ID MDS Sequence Bid Exchange Ask Exchange National BBO Indicator NASDAQ BBO Indicator Quote Cancel/Correction Quote Source TOP OF PAGE What is included in the research IR performs to locate Daubert/adverse motions and orders? The following disclaimer applies to all research that
is performed and we suggest providing a similar disclaimer to
clients when providing any research results : Please note this is not necessarily a complete collection of unfavorable rulings, given limitations surrounding public records searches associated with expert testimony. In addition to IR’s research, we also recommend the case team 1) Check the Challenges and Adverse Rulings folder, 2) review the Expert's Marketing LAN folder, if available, 3) check for and/or complete an Expert Disclosure Checklist with the expert, and 4) check Firm Notes in Interaction+. IR  also will check whether the expert already has Challenges and Adverse Rulings research, available here , and let the team know and/or leverage as needed. I R 's research includes retrieving Daubert Tracker and Westlaw Challenge reports, as well as a keyword searches in Lexis Courtlink, Bloomberg Law, and Lex Machina. Daubert Tracker reports do not have a cost associated with them. Westlaw Challenge reports cost $75 per Expert Challenge Report. These reports capture most adverse rulings, and they can be obtained quickly, but they are not perfect and may miss things occasionally. Expert Witness Profiler report purchases can be obtained for a fee if desired. Expert Exclusion Training : By Serena Thomas on Dec 2, 2025 Preliminary Screening Report Sample : gives you both a snapshot of an expert’s testimonial history and an accurate assessment of how prolific a testifier that expert has been in the past $35 for 2 business day turn around $50 for 1 business day turn around Expert Challenge Study Sample : includes direct challenges to experts as well as instances where the expert’s testimony/ affidavit was submitted in support or against a motion $175 for 3 business day turn around $250 for 1 business day turn around Expert Witness Profile Sample : includes the complete background information on any expert witness including challenge history, testimonial history, personal litigation history, professional history, licenses, certifications, disciplinary actions, political contributions, publications, social media information and more with our flagship Expert Witness Profile. $625 for 7 business day turn around IR can also perform keyword searches to locate adverse rulings if asked to do so: These searches can take hours and/or days depending on how often the expert in question has testified. Keyword searching is limited to Lexis Courtlink, Bloomberg Law, and Lex Machina. IR will provide the motions to exclude, the order on the motion to exclude, if available, and the docket to the team. All research will be saved to the Challenges and Adverse Rulings research folder, available here . If IR estimates it will take more than a few hours to review search results, we will let the team know that they can enlist Orange to perform this research and create or add information to a Challenges & Adverse Rulings summary which is a detailed excel summary of each finding from Daubert Tracker, Westlaw and Lexis Courtlink. Orange's research would need to be billed to a case, Practice Area or other non-billable. Requests to use Orange Research will be referred to Gena Rosati to manage. TOP OF PAGE What are some Beta sources we use? Ibbotson :  Ibbotson Beta Books are published twice a year, but Cornerstone does not subscribe to them.  The Ibbotson Cost of Capital Yearbook has Betas for industries.  The CR library has the editions for 1998 – current. Barra :  The IR staff can retrieve the Barra Beta data for companies from Alacra.  Cost is $80 for one report (one month) for one company or $160 for a range of reports for one company in spreadsheet format. Cost for an industry report is $120 for one month or $240 for a range of months. Bloomberg :  Find Beta using the commands Ticker <Equity Key> Beta Go .  Bloomberg allows you to choose your time period and index for calculating Beta. Yahoo Finance :  After you input your ticker and retrieve your company’s information page click on “Key Statistics” from the left hand tool bar.  Beta will be on the Key Statistics page on the right hand side. This will be the most current Beta. Compustat :  Beta is calculated for a 5-year (60-month) time period.  If less than 60 months of data is available, Beta will be calculated for as few as 24 months.  Month end closing prices (including dividends) are used in the calculation.  Current and historical Beta can be retrieved. Compustat is no longer available, but requests can be made to S&P on a custom basis. Capital IQ :  The current Beta for a company is displayed in the tear sheet under Stock Price and Chart.  Use the Excel add-in to retrieve the historical Beta for any company or group of companies for 1, 2 3, 4, or 5-year Beta.  You will need to add the Historical Beta Calculation template to your excel add-in templates.  Beta for a group of companies can also be retrieved using a company screening search. TOP OF PAGE Are all company SIC codes the same? If you are trying to create a list of companies with the same SIC code, this could be tricky. When a company files reports with the SEC, the company is assigned a SIC code.  It is not common for a company to change the code, because the SEC has to agree to it and it is a long process, but it can happen.  If you look in the header of the filing you will see the SEC assigned SIC code. Most SEC filing forms do not require (or have a space for) primary SIC code.  However, certain registration statements do (such as S-1 and SB-1 and SB-2).  Companies self-designate on their registration statement what they believe their primary SIC code to be.  Based on the first digit of this code, the SEC sends the filing to a particular group to review.  That group will then look at the company's business description, etc. and decide what the SIC code should be based on the company's primary role .  It may be different than what the company says.  The SEC does not appear to require any changes to the form submitted in the event that the SEC feels the code should be something else. Thus, what you see on the registration statement is what the company classified itself to be.  However, the SEC does track SIC codes in its system, and records the code that the SEC believes is correct.  This SEC-designated SIC code is then supplied to Edgar, and is the source of the header information that accompanies every electronic filing stored on Edgar for a company.  If a company wishes to change it’s SIC code as listed in the SEC system and Edgar header file, it must go through a formal review process, fill out forms, etc. with the SEC.  Most information companies such as D&B, GIS, etc. pull their SIC code information from Edgar, but.... Refinitiv Eikon .  Eikon does “value added” services, and reviews things like SIC code themselves.  When they receive a filing for a company, they look at the company's business description and decide on the appropriate SIC code based on which role produces the most revenue for the company.  Sometimes this may differ from the SEC, because it may not be the company's primary role. Capital IQ ’s assigned primary industry for most public and some private companies comes from Standard & Poor's, specifically their GICS product. GICS has a very rigorous process through which they assign and update a GIC (Global Industry Classification) – they look at revenues derived from a business as well as a qualitative review of the companies business, so it's not just a quantitative assignment.  For example, PepsiCo derives most of its revenues from it's bottling business, but S&P has decided that based on the company's actual product line, it should be a soft drink company.  All assignments are passed through a committee that consists of S&P and MSCI staff.  They review/update GICs one or two times a year.  So. . . The S&P indexing team never looks to see what SIC code any company has assigned to itself.  (Usually done with SEC filings.)  They assign each company in the database a GICS code then map the GICS code to the SIC code they believe is most appropriate. TOP OF PAGE How do Thomson SDC industry codes relate to the NAIC and SIC codes? To see a mapping between Thomson's various industry codes and the SIC and NAICS, click here . TOP OF PAGE What is the coverage of online newspapers in our databases? Many of the newspapers we search have articles that appear online, but might not be picked up by the databases we search, such as Factiva or Nexis.  In order to capture these online articles, it is a good idea to go to each newspaper's website, and search the content there.  These online articles might be available for free, or for a fee.  We have compiled a worksheet with more detail concerning online coverage. TOP OF PAGE When was this news publically available? We are working on this page TOP OF PAGE When do I need to purchase copyright permissions ? Copyright permissions a re included in our contracts with JSTOR, Factiva, Refinitiv, CapitalIQ, Thomson, and EBSCO. Obtaining an article through a document delivery service will include the cost of obtaining copyright permission. Documents that are not included in a current Cornerstone contract or subscription will need to address the copyright issue if it is to be used for any Cornerstone project.  This would include downloading articles from Google, SCRIBD, and Harvard case studies. TOP OF PAGE Why does IR warn against purchasing ebooks for case work? Ebooks are almost always licensed only to one person (as opposed to print books, which are subject to copyright law and can be physically moved around because of the First-Sale Doctrine) Ebooks almost always have some form of Digital Rights Management (technology that prevents books from being shared, downloaded, printed, etc.) TOP OF PAGE What does * (an asterisk) in the headline of an article retrieved from Factiva mean? Asterisks indicate that it is a flash headline and
there is no accompanying body text to that item. Flash headlines are generally
the first instance of breaking news. Additional updates with body text will
follow, but flashes are intended to get important news out to newswires users
as quickly as possible TOP OF PAGE How do I produce a link? The Legal Bluebook Quick Style Guide under "internet sources" illustrates how to embed sources in your citations. The Legal Bluebook's Citation Format Examples for Footnotes sample guide may be helpful in providing examples on how to produce links.

Can Factiva search foreign languages?

Yes, Factiva includes publications in 27 non-English languages.  If the language uses lettering that requires a special keyboard or font software (Japanese, Chinese, etc.), someone will need to type the search terms in the foreign language and e-mail them to the IR.  Then the search terms can be cut and pasted into the Factiva search text box.  The results will have to be downloaded in PDF rather than TXT or DOC format.
What’s up with those Factiva timestamps?
Headlines are in ET and full text articles are in GMT.

Some case team members discovered a few unusual inconsistencies with the timestamps of some articles downloaded from Factiva.  While researching these few articles, more and more inconsistencies surfaced.  These issues resulted in a month-long investigation by IR into how timestamps are assigned, where they come from and different publishers’ methods for dealing with updates and corrections.  We talked directly to Factiva developers, and Dow Jones’ and Reuters’ content managers to finally determine how timestamps worked.

Click herefora 6-page document we created to explain all the variances and issues with timestamps in Factiva, Reuters and others.  The first page is an executive summary of the main points, and the rest goes into much detail regarding these points and some others.  If the cases that you work on rely on the timestamps pulled from Factiva, you should try to find some time to go through this document as you may have to make some changes to how you use timestamps and what you assume about them. (LLL 6-12-14)
What types of articles can I exclude from Factiva? Can I exclude republished news, daily market data, obituaries, and other recurring articles?

We can use the codes (not ns=(nnam or nrmf or nrgn)) to exclude hourly share-price stories and republished, or duplicate news items, weather related articles, obituaries and sports articles that may not be relevant to your search.
For Eikon, the default display date is the Published date. In order to find the Availability date, we would have to redo the search to include that field with the output.
Time zone is EST and in a 24-hour format.
Time stamps for reports from Capital IQ are based on when the report was Uploaded to their database.  The time zone is EST.

Goldman Sachs, Citi and B Riley/KBR are not available to us through any databases. These are just a few of the most commonly asked for contributors. To see what contributors are covered, visit theS&P Capital IQandEikonpages.

-The SEC website.  After doing your company search, click on a document.  The first screen you see will have the time for more current filings, about 2002 forward.  In the sample below, the time stamp is seen under SEC Accession No. in the field Accepted.  The time is Eastern Time and is when the SEC received the filing.
Period of Report:2002-12-31Documents:10
See page 8 of thisdocumentfor confirmation of time zone on SEC filings time stamps.

-Information Resources can retrieve a list of all filings plus timestamps from Thomson Research.  This will be the time the filing was posted by Thomson, the closest we can get to the SEC filing time stamp.  The list will be in Excel format.

-Capital IQ also has timestamps.  However, timestamps for SEC filings can be different between the SEC website (EDGAR) and CapIQ.  Specifically, the differences seem to arise when a document is filed with the SEC after about 5:00 pm.  When this happens, the SEC reports the actual time filed, but CapIQ has a timestamp of 6:00 am (or a couple minutes after) on the next day.

What are some Beta sources we use?

Ibbotson:  Ibbotson Beta Books are published twice a year, but Cornerstone does not subscribe to them.  The Ibbotson Cost of Capital Yearbook has Betas for industries.  The CR library has the editions for 1998 – current.

Barra:  The IR staff can retrieve the Barra Beta data for companies from Alacra.  Cost is $80 for one report (one month) for one company or $160 for a range of reports for one company in spreadsheet format.Cost for an industry report is $120 for one month or $240 for a range of months.
Bloomberg:  Find Beta using the commandsTicker<Equity Key>Beta Go.  Bloomberg allows you to choose your time period and index for calculating Beta.

Yahoo Finance:  After you input your ticker and retrieve your company’s information page click on “Key Statistics” from the left hand tool bar.  Beta will be on the Key Statistics page on the right hand side.
This will be the most current Beta.

Compustat:  Beta is calculated for a 5-year (60-month) time period.  If less than 60 months of data is available, Beta will be calculated for as few as 24 months.  Month end closing prices (including dividends) are used in the calculation.  Current and historical Beta can be retrieved.Compustat is no longer available, but requests can be made to S&P on a custom basis.

Capital IQ:  The current Beta for a company is displayed in the tear sheet under Stock Price and Chart.  Use the Excel add-in to retrieve the historical Beta for any company or group of companies for 1, 2 3, 4, or 5-year Beta.  You will need to add the Historical Beta Calculation template to your excel add-in templates.  Beta for a group of companies can also be retrieved using a company screening search.
If you are trying to create a list of companies with the same SIC code, this could be tricky.

When a company files reports with theSEC,the company is assigned a SIC code.  It is not common for a company to change the code, because the SEC has to agree to it and it is a long process, but it can happen.  If you look in the header of the filing you will see the SEC assigned SIC code.

Most SEC filing forms do not require (or have a space for) primary SIC code.  However, certain registration statements do (such as S-1 and SB-1 and SB-2).  Companies self-designate on their registration statement what they believe their primary SIC code to be.  Based on the first digit of this code, the SEC sends the filing to a particular group to review.  That group will then look at the company's business description, etc. and decide what the SIC code should be based on thecompany's primary role.  It may be different than what the company says.  The SEC does not appear to require any changes to the form submitted in the event that the SEC feels the code should be something else.

Thus, what you see on the registration statement is what the company classified itself to be.  However, the SEC does track SIC codes in its system, and records the code that the SEC believes is correct.  This SEC-designated SIC code is then supplied to Edgar, and is the source of the header information that accompanies every electronic filing stored on Edgar for a company.  If a company wishes to change it’s SIC code as listed in the SEC system and Edgar header file, it must go through a formal review process, fill out forms, etc. with the SEC.  Most information companies such as D&B, GIS, etc. pull their SIC code information from Edgar, but....Refinitiv Eikon.  Eikon does “value added” services, and reviews things like SIC code themselves.  When they receive a filing for a company, they look at the company's business description and decide on the appropriate SIC code based onwhich role produces the most revenuefor the company.  Sometimes this may differ from the SEC, because it may not be the company's primary role.

CapitalIQ’s assigned primary industry for most public and some private companies comes from Standard & Poor's, specifically their GICS product. GICS has a very rigorous process through which they assign and update a GIC (Global Industry Classification) – they look at revenues derived from a business as well as a qualitative review of the companies business, so it's not just a quantitative assignment.  For example, PepsiCo derives most of its revenues from it's bottling business, but S&P has decided that based on the company's actual product line, it should be a soft drink company.  All assignments are passed through a committee that consists of S&P and MSCI staff.  They review/update GICs one or two times a year.  So. . . The S&P indexing team never looks to see what SIC code any company has assigned to itself.  (Usually done with SEC filings.)  They assign each company in the database a GICS code then map the GICS code to the SIC code they believe is most appropriate.

What does * (an asterisk) in the headline of an article retrieved from Factiva mean?

Asterisks indicate that it is a flash headline and
there is no accompanying body text to that item. Flash headlines are generally
the first instance of breaking news. Additional updates with body text will
follow, but flashes are intended to get important news out to newswires users
as quickly as possible

Copyright Restrictions To comply with copyright restrictions, the following policies apply on CRIKIT: For Crikit Materials Any materials found on Crikit cannot be included verbatim into any work product. For Academic Literature In general all Academic papers should be added to the Academic Literature section of CRIKIT in the appropriate JEL category using the Academic Paper Template Please provide the link to the source - JSTOR, EBSCO (both available via Library Page on the Portal), SSRN, etc. Once the paper has been added under Academic Literature, you may link to that page from anywhere else in CRIKIT (for example, cite to it (see example)). In the rare instances where you feel the need to upload the paper directly to CRIKIT, please contact the IR  regarding the copyright policies for the paper in question. Please do not upload the paper unless you received an explicit permission from the IR. For Court Opinions If the Court opinion is obtained from the Court's website, you may upload it to CRIKIT directly.  Please provide the link the source (court's page) as appropriate. We cannot upload anything downloaded from Lexis or Westlaw. For Government Reports Please provide a link to the source directly (i.e. FCC page with the report in question) instead of uploading the report to CRIKIT. For Academic Literature
In general all Academic papers should be added to the Academic Literature section of CRIKIT in the appropriate JEL category using the Academic Paper Template

In the rare instances where you feel the need to upload the paper directly to CRIKIT, please contact the IR  regarding the copyright policies for the paper in question.
Please do not upload the paper unless you received an explicit permission from the IR.
For Court Opinions

If the Court opinion is obtained from the Court's website, you may upload it to CRIKIT directly.  Please provide the link the source (court's page) as appropriate. We cannot upload anything downloaded from Lexis or Westlaw.

"CRIKIT" comes fromCR+WIKI+ITas in "Find it!" (and make it snappy - "wiki").

Thanks to Matt Lambert (formerly CRSF) for suggesting the winning entry.

page_41.body_text: ​FAQ FAQ for Bloomberg Data License 1. Pricing/Logistics 1.1. Is there a document with pricing for different data categories? 1.2. When is Cornerstone charged for the data we retrieve? 1.3. If I request a data field that isn’t available for a particular security, am I still charged for the data if it is all “NA”? 1.4. Is it necessary to “save” your data request before submitting? Or will the request still work if you go straight to “submit”? 1.5. Will I be charged for downloading an Excel file directly from the Bloomberg terminal that is not available through the data license? 1.6. If a security has more than 1 CUSIP associated with it; will we be charged for each CUSIP (sometimes 10-15) or by security? 1.7. If you just look up a price on the terminal using the regular BB screen and just view it, (but not download it,) is there an extra charge associated with that? 1.8. We want to download about 4 years of aluminum pricing. Where does commodity pricing fall on the pricing sheet? 1.9. What is the cost of bond ratings data? We are specifically looking for one security's debt ratings by the three major ratings agencies. This should be the "CRSP" function at the Bloomberg terminal. 1.10. How much is it to download 2 years of historical data for the 16 banks involved in setting the 3 month, USD Libor? 1.11. Why can’t I download the following Option Adjusted Corporate Bond Spreads: "C0A1," "C0A4," and "H0A1” from the terminal? 1.12. Are the following part of our data license? .TEDSP Index and .LIBXROI Index? 1.13. How much would it cost to download 4 years of prepayment speed data using the CPH function? 1.14. Where can I find loan level data for Countrywide or other mortgage backed securities? I’ve found the data but cannot download it using the history wizard. Can it be downloaded using the software? 1.15. How much would it cost to download institutional ownership data from Bloomberg? 1.16. How can I download a list of all stocks on the NYSE and NASDAQ, and their market capitalization, as of a specific historical date (i.e. 8/12/05) Also would it cost more to download this data for a time period of several days as opposed to only one day? 1.17. Is downloading news articles from Bloomberg free? 1.18. We need to download daily returns data from Bloomberg for around 15 funds over 2 years. We would like an estimate of what this will cost. 1.19. How much is it to download auction rate security data? 1.20. How much would it cost to download corporate bond pricing data from Bloomberg? 1.21. I am trying to get a price estimate for retrieving the ratings for 350 bonds over 5 years? 1.22. Does downloading a CACS (looking it up on a terminal and outputting to Excel) cost money, beyond the Bloomberg logon fee? 1.23. What is the cost for downloading industry/sector related descriptive fields for a number of different securities? For example, 127 securities for variables (INDUSTRY_SECTOR or INDUSTRY_GROUP) 2. Specifying Downloads/Fields 2.1. How do you enter date ranges when using the download tool? 2.2. Is there a comprehensive list of Getdata fields (there appears to be one for Gethistory in the Data License Per Security Product Manual). Which fields can be downloaded for Getdata but not Gethistory? 2.3. Is there any way the data tool can download descriptive information such as DES screens or News summaries, or does this information need to come from the Bloomberg terminal? 3. Personal Defaults 3.1. According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, it is possible to link the data license account with individual Bloomberg logins, to take advantage of personal defaults.  Will individual Cornerstone users be able to access their personal defaults when using the data download tool? 3.2. According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, the Gethistory program defaults to adjusting volume/price for splits and not dividends. Do personal defaults override the Gethistory defaults?  Is there a way to change these defaults, besides by linking through personal defaults?  Do these defaults apply to the Getdata program, or is price/volume only from Gethistory? 4. Data questions 4.1. What is the Difference between Bloomberg and Markit Short Sales Data 4.2. More questions? Pricing/Logistics Is there a document with pricing for different data categories? Yes. When is Cornerstone charged for the data we retrieve? Bloomberg charges clients when the response file is generated (when a file comes back from the Bloomberg server). By the time the file is opened on the Local side, a charge should be in place. If I request a data field that isn’t available for a particular security, am I still charged for the data if it is all “NA”? No. Is it necessary to “save” your data request before submitting? Or will the request still work if you go straight to “submit”? Yes, you must save the request prior to submitting it. Will I be charged for downloading an Excel file directly from the Bloomberg terminal that is not available through the data license? It is possible to download some data files directly from the Bloomberg terminal that are not available through the data license, and by doing so you will incur only the charge to use the terminal, without any additional fees.  For example, Bloomberg allows you to export the members of an index (such as the NYA NYSE Composite Index) into an Excel file straight from the Terminal without an additional fee.  Before downloading this type of data, you should contact #Bloomberg Software Help on a case-by-case basis to determine if there are applicable charges. If a security has more than 1 CUSIP associated with it; will we be charged for each CUSIP (sometimes 10-15) or by security? We do count each individual CUSIP as a unique security, so each collateral level would incur that $2.00 fee. If you just look up a price on the terminal using the regular BB screen and just view it, (but not download it,) is there an extra charge associated with that? There is no charge for what we consider "view only" data on the terminal. However, please note the following: If this is data that can be downloaded through the new software but you do it through the terminal instead, be warned that if it is a lot of data, they will shut down the terminal and will not turn it back on for at least a month. We also risk losing our Bloomberg license altogether if we regularly try to get around their system. We want to download about 4 years of aluminum pricing. Where does commodity pricing fall on the pricing sheet? Commodities fall under the equities category (listed there as futures). For historical data however, the charge of $3.00 is the same regardless of the security type. What is the cost of bond ratings data? We are specifically looking for one security's debt ratings by the three major ratings agencies. This should be the "CRSP" function at the Bloomberg terminal. Ratings data is a little tricky as all 3 major agencies, S&P, Moody's and Fitch keep a tight lid on how their data is disseminated. Data can be pulled for up to 500 securities per month for Moody's and S&P without requiring an additional license with them directly. How much is it to download 2 years of historical data for the 16 banks involved in setting the 3 month, USD Libor? The cost will be $3 per security for which you are downloading historical data. Why can’t I download the following Option Adjusted Corporate Bond Spreads: "C0A1," "C0A4," and "H0A1” from the terminal? Unfortunately these securities are not downloadable off of the terminal. These securities were created and are maintained by Merrill Lynch and as part of their agreement to house this data on the system, data for these securities are not downloadable through data license or API. Are the following part of our data license? .TEDSP Index and .LIBXROI Index? Yes, these do in fact fall under the "Equities, Options, Futures, Warrants, Funds, Index and Currencies" category for a $3.00 charge. How much would it cost to download 4 years of prepayment speed data using the CPH function? Historical prepayment speeds can be downloaded in bulk through the historical time series option in our getdata program. This is charged at a rate of $3.00 per security. Where can I find loan level data for Countrywide or other mortgage backed securities? I’ve found the data but cannot download it using the history wizard. Can it be downloaded using the software? Unfortunately this information is currently not available through data license (or API) at this time. How much would it cost to download institutional ownership data from Bloomberg? Unfortunately, we do not have holdings data available through data license at this time. We will be sure to inform you should this become available through data license. However it can be viewed on screen using the HDS function on the terminal. How can I download a list of all stocks on the NYSE and NASDAQ, and their market capitalization, as of a specific historical date (i.e. 8/12/05) Also would it cost more to download this data for a time period of several days as opposed to only one day? There are approximately 5100 securities that trade on the NYSE and first tier NasdaQ: If you need just pricing for one particular day in time that could be obtained through our single point history feature at a cost of $0.20 a security. Since market cap was also mentioned, the only method of pulling that data point historically is through our gethistory program at a cost of $3.00 a security. Since the gethistory program does not distinguish between 1 day of history or 10 years, additional history could be pulled on that security list and still remain within the $3.00 charge. Is downloading news articles from Bloomberg free? There is no additional cost beyond the $150 login. We need to download daily returns data from Bloomberg for around 15 funds over 2 years. We would like an estimate of what this will cost. The cost will be $3 per fund assuming they are funds whose info is basic and publically available. How much is it to download auction rate security data? Pricing for these securities would depend on the type of security that they are pulling. This information would cost the following on a per security basis: Corporates, Money Markets, Governments: $1.50 Municipals: $1.00 Agency Pools: $0.15 CMO, CMBS, Whole Loans and ABS: $2.00 How much would it cost to download corporate bond pricing data from Bloomberg? It depends on the bond.  If they are just basic bonds that are generally available (i.e. not illiquid) and you are just getting pricing then it is either $3 per bond if you are getting the history (gethistory function), or $.60 per bond if you are just getting a few days.  That is per bond, not per day. I am trying to get a price estimate for retrieving the ratings for 350 bonds over 5 years? Unfortunately, ratings are not available to be downloaded historically. Does downloading a CACS (looking it up on a terminal and outputting to Excel) cost money, beyond the Bloomberg logon fee? the charge is $1.50 per security for Corporate and Government securities. This is the charge incurred when using the data license software.  If you are able to export a screen directly from the Bloomberg terminal, there is no additional charge for that.  Basically, if you want just a few companies, you'd probably want to use the export function from the terminal.  If you wanted the CACS for a few hundred companies, the data license is more cost efficient in terms of time. What is the cost for downloading industry/sector related descriptive fields for a number of different securities? For example, 127 securities for variables (INDUSTRY_SECTOR or INDUSTRY_GROUP) The cost would be $1.50 per security regardless of whether you requested one or both of those fields. Specifying Downloads/Fields How do you enter date ranges when using the download tool? You can just use date range in some programs as gethistory, getticks, getquotes, getallticks, getallquotes, getactions and getfundamental. If you are using request builder you can use the calendar on the bottom, if you are writing your request you just need to include DATERANGE= on your header (see page 18 of the Per Security manual for more details) Is there a comprehensive list of Getdata fields (there appears to be one for Gethistory in the Data License Per Security Product Manual). Which fields can be downloaded for Getdata but not Gethistory? There is a file that is updated daily on our server called “fields.csv.”  This lists all of the fields with their field types. Gethistory is mainly for historical prices. Is there any way the data tool can download descriptive information such as DES screens or News summaries, or does this information need to come from the Bloomberg terminal? Info that appears on DES screens may be accessed through Per Security requests, however, there is not a request type per say that will fully encompass all data that appears on a DES screen without individually selecting each data point in the file. News may not be accessed through Data License Per Security, however, there is a news feed product we offer as a separate license. Personal Defaults According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, it is possible to link the data license account with individual Bloomberg logins, to take advantage of personal defaults.  Will individual Cornerstone users be able to access their personal defaults when using the data download tool? The Cornerstone Bloomberg terminals are shared terminals, however, they may be linked to Request Builder software in order to set overrides (i.e. specific pricing sources, distributions, fundamental analysis, etc). Split-adjusted and not split-adjusted share price defaults may be set on the Terminal through the PDFE<GO> function.  Choose 6<GO> and at the bottom of the page you’ll see an area to set Capital Changes Defaults. In order to link to a terminal, you will type “IAM” and press enter on the terminal.  This will give you a User # and S/N.  This info may be entered in the “Optional Parameter” area under the Settings tab on the Request Builder Login screen. N.B. that this will change the defaults for all users of your data license terminal, so use this option carefully (i.e. switch back to standard defaults before logging off). According to the Data License Per Security Product Manual, the Gethistory program defaults to adjusting volume/price for splits and not dividends. Do personal defaults override the Gethistory defaults?  Is there a way to change these defaults, besides by linking through personal defaults?  Do these defaults apply to the Getdata program, or is price/volume only from Gethistory? The only way to have your personal default attached to DL is by linking your request to a Terminal. You can run getdata also linked, all your set ups will be applied in this case (pricing source, PDFE, PDFN, etc). · Data License defaults . · Adjustments that can/cannot be made by linking to PDF are here (see columns F-J). Data questions What is the Difference between Bloomberg and Markit Short Sales Data? There are three main reasons for the differences, all of which relate to how Bloomberg gets its data vs. Markit.  Bloomberg gets its data from the exchange and the reporting entities are U.S. broker dealers.  Markit gets its data from its global clients (custodians, prime brokers, hedge funds), which give Markit data on their securities lending activity (custodian), securities borrowing activity (prime brokers), and cost of borrowing (hedge funds).  Markit uses its proprietary data on securities lending to proxy for short interest whereas Bloomberg gives the reported numbers.  The reasons for the data differences are: Bloomberg’s data includes naked shorts, which option market makers are allowed to do.  Since shares are not borrowed in this scenario, Markit data would not reflect it. When an investor (e.g., a hedge fund) wants to short, it will go to its prime broker to borrow shares.  Depending on the situation, the prime broker may lend out shares from its own inventory (e.g., from their proprietary trading desk) rather than go out and borrow shares from a custodian.  This usually makes the cost of borrowing lower, but tends to happen only for blue chip stocks where shares are plentiful.  This type of shorting would be reported in Bloomberg’s data, but not in Markit’s (presumably because the prime broker didn’t actually borrow shares). Markit’s clients are global and includes firms that do not report to the exchange.  For example, if a foreign firm wants to short a U.S. stock, that would not be reported in Bloomberg, but would potentially be captured by Markit. More questions? Email your Bloomberg contacts .

page_43.body_text: BranDwatch Source Brandwatch How to Cite the Source Brandwatch Consumer Research Description Brandwatch is a leading provider of social and business analytics software that enables major enterprises to answer critical business questions using insights derived from social and enterprise data. Powered by a broad array of patented analytics technologies and the largest library of social data in the market with more than 750 billion posts, Crimson's platform is used by hundreds of leading global organizations. A simplified description of their methodology can be found here . Brandwatch Consumer Research Features.pdf The list of blogs and news sites is a sample of what Brandwatch collects not the entire list as they aggregate public sites daily.  They gather over 105 million sites from the web, so they do not have a full list of blogs and news forums. Demo of Brandwatch Resources Site Coverage overview Selection of Social Network, News and Blog Coverage How we gather data Metadata table Historical data Time Period Covered Data from 1986 to current are available as quarterly datasets in compressed zip files. To receive updates when new data are available, click on the link to the subscription form, in the sidebar to the right, and select "Financial Holding Company Data" from the list of subscriptions. Access Contact #Information Resources Contact Information Resources Cost Cost for one month of access per case team: 1-3 active queries and up to 3 users = $2,000 4- 6 active queries and up to 4 ausers = $4,000 7- 9 active queries and up to 4 users = $6,000 10-12 active queries and up to 4 users = $8,000 * Teams can create more than the above numbers of queries, but active ones are limited to thresholds above because Cornerstone only has so many available One-off queries run by IR: $250 per inquiry - billed by query not by content source. Data would be both volume summary stats and also raw posts (up to 5,000) matching your search term. Must be a discretely defined one-off query in terms of date parameter, social media sources requested, and keyword query If raw post search results are requested, these should not exceed 5,000 posts (our daily limit is 100,000 total/50,000 for Twitter) Important Notes Our Twitter export limit is 50,000 (firm-wide, per day).  We get a total of 100k exports per day into CSV (up to 50,000 Twitter mentions). Please reach out to #Brandwatch Users to coordinate large exports. Important changes to Reddit data usage in Brandwatch Due to a Reddit Terms of Service update, Brandwatch must now redact certain fields in API responses and exports. You can still view Reddit posts and comments within the Brandwatch platform. You cannot export or distribute Reddit post text, comments, or author names outside of Brandwatch. Previous reports using Reddit data are not affected, but please ensure recently downloaded data is not used in external deliverables. For questions or concerns, contact Thomas Powell (Legal), Gena Rosati (Information Resources), and Mark D'Agostino (Data Science Center). See the Reddit Compliance – Consumer Research.pdf for a full list of affected fields. AI Restrictions At Cornerstone we Cannot use Brandwatch data to "train, develop, enhance, or contribute to any generative artificial intelligence models, machine learning models, or any form of algorithmic or software-based artificial intelligence systems" without pre-approval from Brandwatch. Brandwatch's Service Appendix AI Definitions/Capabilities Definition of Artificial Intelligence : "intelligence displayed by machines, in contrast with the natural intelligence displayed by humans and other animals." IRIS : AI tool created by Brandwatch that "automatically analyzes your data and spots any significant spike... It then reads all of the metrics and tries to discover the key drivers of conversation." Uses social media, newsletters, to get data Compares this to 20 days of historical data to see spike in brand usage Presents data clear and simple on right hand side of the screen Runs search on all of your data over every spike Part of already existing platform Way to benchmark, check your work, and be more time efficient React Score : AI-powered tool that identifies "online conversations that could impact your brand reputation" Updated 6/25/2026_hg

CLE ON THE LAN 2.5. APPLICATION FEES 2.6. FEDEX 2.7. MAINTAINING APPLICATION RECORDS 3. POST-EVENT CLE PROCESSING 3.1. ATTENDANCE SHEETS 3.2. CERTIFICATES OF ATTENDANCE 3.2.1. New York 3.2.2. California 3.2.3. Illinois 3.2.4. Delaware 3.2.5. Virginia 3.2.6. Pennsylvania 3.2.7. New Hampshire 3.2.8. Email Template 3.2.9. Reporting Attendance Electronically 3.2.9.1. Texas State Bar MCLE Site for Providers 3.3. MAINTAINING ATTENDANCE RECORDS Introduction to MCLE The following U.S. states and territories require lawyers to take mandatory or minimum continuing legal education (MCLE) courses in order to practice law within that particular jurisdiction. Summary of MCLE Jurisdiction Requirements Credit Hours Defined As of January 2010, the following jurisdictions have a 60-minute credit hour: (States to which we commonly apply are in bold, blue font) AK, AL, AZ, AR, BC, CA , DE , GA, ID, IL , IN, IA, KY, LA, ME, MN, MS, MT, NH , NV, NC, ND, NM, OH, OR, PA , PR, QC, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA , VT, WA and WY. As of October 2007, the following jurisdictions have a 50-minute credit hour: CO, FL, GU, KS, MO, NY , OK, RI, VI, WV and WI. Preparing for a CLE event STANDARD COURSE APPLICATIONS The location of the event determines the states to which we will automatically apply for course approval California events require no applications as we are a preferred provider New York events require no applications as we are a preferred provider Washington, DC and Delaware both require applications to VA, DE,& PA PA applications are processed after the event due to advertising requirements. Chicago events require applications to IL Massachusetts events require an application to NH For guidance on creating new MCLE courses, see the rules and regulations for each state governing MCLE.  For the seven states listed above, a summary document was created for reference. RULE OF 5 If an event has 5 or more attorneys from a state to which we do not apply automatically (i.e. five attorneys from IL come to a NY event), we will apply for course approval in that state. ATTORNEY REQUEST If an attorney asks us to apply for course approval in his/her state, we will do so as a courtesy. CLE ON THE LAN The LAN folder \\Crwadmin1\marketing\Events\Client is organized by location, then year, the practice area, then speaker.  For instance, when speaking of the 2010 DC Grundfest Securities breakfast, the folder will be here: \\Crwadmin1\marketing\Events\Client\Washington,DC\2010\Securities\Grundfest Within each event’s LAN folder, you will find all the essential documents needed to complete a course application Event invite (brochure) – This PDF lists the location, time, duration, and presenters. Handouts – Some applications require sample materials.  Some require only a Table of Contents.  Always follow the directions on the application. When uncertain, refer to previous course applications for guidance. Some elements common to all of our MCLE-eligible marketing events: Session format – (Live, in-person, faculty in room, etc.) All of our sessions are 120 minutes which calculates to 2 credit hours for both 50-minute credit hours and 60-minute credit hours Handouts are administered in both print and electronic format Our programs are intended for all attorney experience levels We do not have admissions restrictions We do not offer in-house programs Our sessions are evaluated by participant critique (feedback forms) By being approved providers, all of our programs are automatically approved in CA and NY When completing applications, always indicate Charles Cobbins, Director of Marketing as the contact or “sponsor representative” and have Charles sign all necessary forms. APPLICATION FEES If application fees are required by check, submit a check request to Accounts Payable. The request form is on CRIKIT http://crikit/Project_Support/Electronic_Request_Forms/Check_Request_Form Submit a copy of the application to AP along with the check request Charge the practice area who will be hosting the event. For example, a check request a for securities breakfast would use the GL code 9451 COR 5560 (which is Practice Development–Securities–Marketing Events COR Other Expenses) FEDEX Fedex request forms are also on CRIKIT http://crikit/Project_Support/Electronic_Request_Forms/FedEx_Form Similarly, charge to practice area. For example, 9451 COR 5151 (5151 is the GL sub-code for Fedex/Shipping Charges) MAINTAINING APPLICATION RECORDS Maintain copies of all submitted applications, check requests, and Fedex requests on the LAN in an appropriately labeled MCLE sub-folder. For example, \\Crwadmin1\marketing\Events\Client\Washington,DC\2010\Energy\MCLE\Applications If the folder does not have an Applications sub-folder (or Check Request or Fedex sub-folder), create one. Maintain copies of all course approvals (as they are received) on the LAN in the event’s “Approvals” subfolder.  For example, \\Crwadmin1\marketing\Events\Client\Washington,DC\2010\Energy\MCLE\Approvals POST-EVENT CLE PROCESSING ATTENDANCE SHEETS After the event, the event coordinator will send you the attendance sheet and generate a spreadsheet that contains all the information necessary to create the required “Certificates of Attendance” In general, you'll need attorney names, bar ID numbers, and the state for which they would like CLE credit CERTIFICATES OF ATTENDANCE New York As an accredited provider, all attorneys receive a New York Certificate of Attendance regardless of the location of the program.  A template to use in a Word mail merge is available. page_47.body_text: ​(20120118) Capital IQ Excel Plug-In Billing--How to enter the correct billing code From: Londa, Laura To: #Analysts < Analysts@cornerstone.com >; #Associates < Associates@cornerstone.com > Since we have added a lot of new users to Capital IQ, I thought it would be a good time to make sure everyone understands how to enter in a billing code when using the Excel add-in.  Please see below. --Laura ______________________________________________ From: Londa, Laura Sent: Thursday, May 07, 2009 3:27 PM To: #Analysts; #Associates Cc: #Information Resources; Patrick, Jonathan Subject: Capital IQ Excel Plug-In Billing Hello all, I wanted to make sure that everyone who is using Capital IQ's excel plug-in realized that you can set a project code in it or change a previously entered code.  This past month it looks like a lot of people either didn't enter anything (which takes an extroardinary amount of time to research and fix) or didn't realize they could change it and it got billed to the wrong case.  To change the account code please do the following: When you start your work in the Excel plug-in there is an entry box on the top middle of the Excel menu (see below).  Click on the Enable Expense Code button and then enter the code and press Enter.  The code will remain in the box while you work.  Once you use the code once it will get stored in the drop down for next time.  Please don't hesitate to contact me with and questions or concerns. --Laura Laura L. page_51.body_text: (20100105) Changes to Institutional Ownership Data From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, As many of you know we normally get our Insitutional Ownership data from Thomson's ShareWorld product.  Thomson is getting ready to sunset that software and switch over to their online OneBanker product for this data.  There are a few differences that I will go over in this email as well as point you to locations on Crikit for more information.  We have been working with the Securities Practice area to make the transition as smooth as possible.  All changes take effect immediately. Here are the details: We will be retrieving the data from Thomson One Banker [TOB].  This is the same provider we've used previously, but the platform and format will be different.  See file here: < http://crikit/@api/deki/files/2510/=SW-TOB_comparison.xls > for a comparison of the format changes.  With a few exceptions, most requests will be fulfilled using the Single Security Momentum report from TOB.  As well, the major changes between ShareWorld (our previous database) and TOB are detailed here: < http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_by_Subject/Equity_Information/Institutional_Ownership_Data > which includes an FAQ and Glossary. The major change in format will be the inclusion of additional data columns which will be incorporated into the new macro that is part of the float template as well as some additional owners rather than just 13-F filers. Please note that there will be instances in which the data will need to be downloaded from a different module on TOB -- these will come from the Historical Momentum module.  This format is exactly that which we've previously received from ShareWorld (note that the new macro will also parse these files). The Float Template has been updated with the macro that allows one to work with the new (as well as the old) format. PRICING - Cost will be $500 for most data downloads.  However, we are willing to make adjustments for extremes, i.e., if a case only purchased 1 or 2 quarters we would cut it in half, and if they purchased more than 20 we would double it.  There are few cases that fall into those categories so it wouldn't involve too many manual changes for us.  This price has been determined by looking at the average cost of downloads per case. Please feel free to contact #Information Resources if you need more information about Thomson One Banker.  For questions about the Float Template, you should contact #Patriot Pro Help or Larry Dworkin or Kersi Shroff, both in CRNY. Thanks, The Information Resources Department Laura L. page_52.body_text: ​(20100108) Big Changes to Bloomberg--Please Read! From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, We have recently had to renegotiate our Bloomberg license for compliance reasons.  In order to download, save and share Bloomberg data with each other, we have entered into a Data License with Bloomberg.  For an additional cost, there will be a separate piece of software installed on each terminal that will allow you to more easily download data from Bloomberg.  You will still be able to use the regular Bloomberg interface, but will also have an alternative for downloading large quantities of data. What this means is that ALL data downloaded from Bloomberg (via the software OR the regular interface OR Excel) will be charged on a per security, and in some cases per day, basis.  We will pass these costs directly through to the client each month.  As a result, you will need to be very aware of what you are getting from Bloomberg and calculating how much it will cost before you go in to download.  In some cases the costs will be minimal, in others they can quickly reach five or six figures. I will be holding a 30 minute informational session to go over pricing and the upcoming migration each day next week.  After that I will be scheduling training for the software to occur in each office over the next 3 weeks.  We will arrange at least 2 trainings in each office.  While I recommend that anyone who uses or asks for Bloomberg data for their cases attend one of the informational sessions, these sessions and the later training sessions will be REQUIRED for all Analysts (as the primary users of Bloomberg). I will send out 5 invites for the information sessions.  Please just sign up for whichever one is most convenient.  If you cannot make the one you choose, you are welcome to attend one of the others.  They will all be conference calls.  The sessions are: Monday, 1/11 3pm PST (6pm EST); Tuesday, 1/12 10am PST (1pm EST); Wednesday, 1/13 12pm PST (3pm EST); Thursday, 1/14 10am PST (1pm EST); Friday, 1/15 1pm PST (4pm EST). Thank you for your help with this transition, Laura Laura L. page_53.body_text: ​(20100311) Compustat CapIQ and Analyst Reports--Together at Last! From: Londa, Laura To: #Consulting Staff < #ConsultingStaff@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < #InformationResources@cornerstone.com >; Hunter, Kevin < khunter@cornerstone.com >; Wilson, James < jwilson@cornerstone.com >; #AMC < #AMC@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone. Big changes happening here at the Stone.  I think everyone will be happy about most, but there will be a price increase for Compustat that you will want to know about, so read on! Compustat After a year of fumbling through the networked version of Compustat on the term server, we are finally getting easier access.  Compustat data, including the Classic "as-is" data, will now be accessible through Capital IQ and the excel add-in.  The term server version will go down as soon as Kevin Hunter sees this email. LOL (Thank you Kevin for keeping that software alive as long as you did!) You will need to use a different userid and password than your personal one to access the Compustat data.  This is because of the cost of the data. Compustat will now be charged at $2000 per download. There is no charge for searching.  The charge occurs only with downloading data.  I know this seems exceptionally high, but it is based on the cost of the data which has skyrocketed over the years. If you go into Compustat using one of these passwords, please remember to change your password back to your personal password when you go in to regular Capital IQ to avoid overbilling your client.  Each office has been assigned two UserID's (see the end of this email).  Please use one of the ID's associated with your office so as to avoid log-in issues. Analyst Reports We have opened up CapIQ's Investment Research section to the entire firm. If you have a CapIQ ID you can access this new section now.  If you do not, contact #Information Resources to get you one! When you search a company in CapIQ and you scroll down all the list of options on the left you will see a section entitled Research.  Click on Investment Research and you will see the latest analyst reports that CapIQ has.  You can change the date range and add other criteria if you expand the Search Criteria section.  The reports go back well into the 1990's These reports do have additional costs associated with them.  On the left you will see a pdf icon with a $.  Hover over it and it will tell you how much each report is.  Your case will be charged for any you view or download.  The costs vary from $10 to $5000+. While CapIQ and Investext do overlap, you will see many reports that are not found in the other, so it is good to check both if you are concerned with finding everything.  If you have any questions regarding this, do not hesitate to contact #Information Resources with questions. Over the next few months we will hold new Capital IQ training sessions to show you Compustat, Analyst Reports, and many of the other great features available in this database.  It is well worth checking out as there is a wealth of information and data available here.
