page_59.body_text: ​(20100924) New Resource Opened up to Firm: Science Direct From: #Information Resources To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello there. I want to let everyone know that we have been able to open up access to the Science Direct database firm-wide.  The database is IP authenticated so you must be either in the office or on a term server to access.  This database contains the full text of more than 2,500 peer-reviewed journals (including the Journal of Financial Economics) and more than 11,000 books (that you can access by chapter or by book).  It includes historical access to the journals as well, with some going back as far as the early 1800's.  Below is a longer description of this database. When you find an article you wish to read, you will be required to enter your name, email and a cost code .  This code must contain alpha-numeric characters only (no periods or dashes or spaces).  The client will be charged $25 for each article downloaded or viewed.  Books vary in cost .  This database is not flat subscription.  It is pay-as-you-go so the charges are hard costs and Cornerstone will be paying for any articles not billed to a case.  Please keep this in mind as you select articles for downloading.  If you would like any more information or a quick tour of the database, please don't hesitate to ask. To get started, just go here: http://www.sciencedirect.com/ , and if you'd like to browse their list of publications, you can go here: http://www.info.sciverse.com/sciencedirect/content/journals/titles .  This information is also on the ScienceDirect Crikit page here: http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/ScienceDirect Enjoy, Laura About ScienceDirect ScienceDirect is a leading full-text scientific database offering journal articles and book chapters from more than 2,500 peer-reviewed journals and more than 11,000 books. There are currently more than 9.5 million articles/chapters, a content base that is growing at a rate of almost 0.5 million additions per year. Elsevier has digitized as much of the pre 1995 journal owned-content as possible, bringing articles from as far back as 1823 (The Lancet) to the desktop. Never has in-depth literature searching been so comprehensive and easy to find. The platform offers sophisticated search and retrieval functionality that enables the user to maximize the effectiveness of their knowledge discovery process. New tools facilitate research work flow aids such as access to content at an early publication stage and efficient multiple document downloading of content that can be stored, printed and passed to colleagues. The web environment offers new ways to present information as well as enhancing it with other content sources based on semantic technologies, e.g., NextBio. In addition, since 2003, many authors have been submitting extra value-added content associated with the research, such as audio and video files, datasets and other supplementary content, effectively accelerating research beyond the print format. page_63.body_text: (20090505) Reminder: Capturing codes in CRSP From: Londa, Laura To: #Analysts < Analysts@cornerstone.com >; #Associates < Associates@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello all, I'd like to remind everyone that if you are going into CRSP to download data, please be sure to pick the case name as opposed to "No Case Name."  The list is updated regularly and should have all current names.  Should you be downloading for a case that has not been given a name yet (or it has not yet been listed), please send me or #Information Resources an email telling us what the name should be or that it should be billable and to check back with you later.  It takes and extraordinary amount of time for us to look up each user to determine what the data should be billed to. For example, in April alone 55% of the downloads in CRSP were listed as No Case Name.  Of those listed, 62% of them actually had case names that were on the list to be chosen.  I will also work to see if we can add the practice areas to the list since about 20% belonged to a practice area.  It would be a huge help for us if you could take a quick second to find your case name in the list and choose it before entering CRSP or send us an email if you don't find it.  Thanks so much for your understanding and help with this. --A very grateful IR group.  :-) Laura L. I'd like to remind everyone that if you are going into CRSP to download data, please be sure to pick the case name as opposed to "No Case Name."  The list is updated regularly and should have all current names.  Should you be downloading for a case that has not been given a name yet (or it has not yet been listed), please send me or #Information Resources an email telling us what the name should be or that it should be billable and to check back with you later.  It takes and extraordinary amount of time for us to look up each user to determine what the data should be billed to.

For example, in April alone 55% of the downloads in CRSP were listed as No Case Name.  Of those listed, 62% of them actually had case names that were on the list to be chosen.  I will also work to see if we can add the practice areas to the list since about 20% belonged to a practice area.  It would be a huge help for us if you could take a quick second to find your case name in the list and choose it before entering CRSP or send us an email if you don't find it.  Thanks so much for your understanding and help with this.
--A very grateful IR group.  :-)
Laura L. LondaDirector of Information Resources

page_65.body_text: ​(20090625) Some newish and old litigation reporters you might not know we have From: Londa, Laura To: #Officers < #Officers@cornerstone.com >; #Principals < #Principals@cornerstone.com >; #Managers < #Managers@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < #InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello there, I wanted to tell you about some reporters that we have.  Some are new and some we have had but no one is on the routing list, so I thought I'd mention them with a description.  If you would like to be added to the routing list, you can either go to the IR Portal page and click on Routing List in the bar, or just respond to this email and let me know which ones you want to be added to. --Laura Bankruptcy Litigation Reporter Description This reporter offers comprehensive coverage of significant disputes in ongoing bankruptcy proceedings. The editors track dockets, summarizing recent developments and their implications for the debtor, its creditors, officers and directors, employees, and other parties. This reporter covers a wide range of topics, regarding Chapter 11 proceedings and includes analysis of the most noteworthy case law. Important litigation documents are also included. Features Covers significant federal district and appellate court rulings in bankruptcy cases Offers valuable commentaries by practitioners in the field Reviews a wide range of bankruptcy topics in a timely, unbiased manner Covers trial court proceedings, appellate briefings, and U.S. Supreme Court petitions in significant cases Pharmaceutical Litigation Reporter Description This publication provides up-to-date information on developments in litigation, legislation and regulation involving the pharmaceutical industry, with reproductions of the leading court opinions, complaints, briefs and responses. The lawsuits covered range from product liability suits to patent infringement, and from wrongful death to FDA approval. This publication is critical to anyone who needs to keep up-to-date on: FDA regulation, negligence and standards of care, generic competition, Daubert issues, trade secrets, and wrongful death. Intellectual Property Counselor Description This newsletter covers trade secrets, confidential information, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, basic patent information, and Internet and technology issues, all with a focus on providing practical material for corporate counsel. Issues also feature recent developments and useful articles, forms, and checklists. Features Discussion on recent case law and statutory developments Provides timely articles, forms, and checklists covering intellectual property law useful in the day-to-day counseling of businesses Coverage includes trade secrets, confidential information, copyrights, trademarks, licensing, basic patent information, and Internet and technology issues Expert & Scientific Evidence Reporter Description This reporter offers coverage of significant litigation involving how courts interpret the Daubert and Frye standards regarding the admission of expert and scientific testimony. It covers all stages of litigation, from complaint to final appellate decision and each issue. It is a source for determining which evidence courts are likely to allow and which evidence courts tend to disallow, which is especially important in situations where there may be conflicting opinions within the scientific community about the same subject. It covers both federal and state cases on all major issues in this area. Features Includes important documents Covers cases involving products liability, personal injury, antitrust, medical malpractice, asbestos, business/commercial, environmental, family, and criminal law issues Health Affairs Description Health Affairs is the leading journal of health policy thought and research. The peer-reviewed journal was founded in 1981 under the aegis of Project HOPE, a nonprofit international health education organization. Health Affairs explores health policy issues of current concern in both domestic and international spheres. Inside the Journal: Health Affairs is divided into the following major sections: Feature articles: New proposals, original research, and analysis of timely health policy issues Report From The Field: High-level journalistic article that explores a timely health policy topic, published with support of the Kaiser Family Foundation and Kaiser Health Reporting Commentary: Opinions and proposals for change Interviews: Conversations with leaders in government and the private sector Narrative Matters: Personal stories about the health care system that highlight policy issues of concern, published with support of the W.K. Kellogg Foundation Health Tracking: New research on trends and health care markets DataWatch: Data-driven analysis and original research GrantWatch: A review of recently awarded foundation grants and grant outcomes, with regular essays or special reports about health philanthropy Book Reviews Letters to the Editor: Lively discussion of issues raised in Health Affairs papers Thematic Issues: Health Affairs publishes both thematic and “variety” issues every year. Thematic issues (up to five per year) are devoted to in-depth exploration of a key topic surrounding health and health care. Laura L. page_66.body_text: ​(20090720) 3 new databases in the areas of Auditing/Accounting, Poison Pills, and Mergers! From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello everyone, Wanted to let you know about three new databases that we have pay-as-you-go access to.  Below is a brief description and a link to more information and pricing on CRIKIT. Audit Analytics-- Audit Analytics is a public company intelligence service providing independent research to the investment, accounting, insurance, legal, regulatory and academic communities.  Audit Analytics provides detailed research on over 20,000 public companies and more than 1,500 accounting firms.  Not only can you find out which auditors companies are using, but it also tracks when those auditor changes and why.  You can find auditor fees, audit opinions, when companies have issued financial restatements in the past and why, auditor info on deals and issuances, and much much more.  See the page on Crikit for more information: http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Audit_Analytics SharkRepellent-- SharkRepellent from Factset gives in-depth research on US public companies' takeover defense strategies. They cover the companies charters, bylaw provisions, poison pill provisions and state takeover statutes.  You can search on over 200 takeover defense data points.  They also have research covering proxy proposals, proxy fights and activism as well as profiles on activist hedge funds.  Reports can be produced in PDF, Word and Excel and there are direct links to the SEC filings and to the specific part of the filing you are most interested in.  See the page on Crikit for more information including pricing and a samples of their reports. http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Shark_Repellent MergerMetrics-- MergerMetrics from Factset gives in-depth research on Mergers involving US Targets.  Their data includes fees, termination rights, force-the-vote provisions, go-shop provisions, special committees, controlling shareholders, indemnification provisions, and much much more.  You can not only search for deals that have certain conditions, but you can also search for deals that do not have certain conditions.  For example you can create a list of deals that do not have go-shop clause.  The limitations on this database is that it only includes deals where the merger agreement is made available.  As a result you can create a report that contains sections of the agreements or the agreements in their entirety.  You can also report on trends in mergers.  It is an excellent complement to our other merger databases such as SDC and Capital IQ.  See the page on Crikit for more information including pricing and sample reports. http://crikit/Information_Resources/Data_Sources/Data_Sources_Alphabetically/Merger_Metrics If you have any questions about these databases, please do not hesitate to contact me or anyone in Information Resources. --Laura Laura L. page_69.url: https://cresearch3.sharepoint.com/sites/CRIKIT_ZZLibraryInsider/SitePages/(20090723) Some Clarification RE; New Pricing for Bloomberg and Compustat effective August 1.aspx
page_69.body_text: ​(20090723) Some Clarification RE: New Pricing for Bloomberg and Compustat effective August 1 From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < #CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > Hello all, I got several variations of one question several times and so I thought it would make sense to send out a clarification regarding it.  The question was basically what do I put in as a charge code if I do not want the login charged to the client because it is a redo of what I've already done, or there was a mistake in my original download, etc.? Obviously we want to avoid billing the client for our mistakes or excessively for these databases, which is why we put the cap in place on Bloomberg.  I found that the monthly max generally covered the additional logins that were do-overs or fixing mistakes.  However we still want to be sure.  Compustat does not have a cap as it is not used that much, but we will watch it closely and the same rules apply to it. Regardless of why you think the client should not be billed the best thing for you to do is to put in the client code for which you are doing the work.  If, at the end of your work, you still feel the client should not be billed please send an email to #Information Resources, and let us know which database you were on, the date on it and what the code was you put in.  We will take care of correcting the allocations at month end.  This way is MUCH MORE efficient than putting in a generic code which raises all sorts of red flags and causes us in IR to do a lot of additional work at month-end.  So please always remember to put in the code for whatever case, or non-billable project you are doing the work for. BTW this also applies to all other databases that request codes such as Westlaw Business, Capital IQ, CRSP, etc.  You can always tell us the client shouldn't be billed afterwards. Thanks so much for your understanding, and do not hesitate to email me if you have any questions. _____________________________________________ From: Londa, Laura Sent: Tuesday, July 21, 2009 1:17 PM To: #Cornerstone Research Subject: New Pricing for Bloomberg and Compustat effective August 1 Hello everyone, After evaluating usage over 4 weeks we have determined that the best pricing in order to recover our costs and protect our clients from excessive charges is as follows: Bloomberg: $100/login  Cap at $1000 per month Compustat: $500/login no cap at this time This pricing will begin on August 1st.  Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions. --Laura Laura L. page_77.body_text: ​(20081223) Compustat is back From: Londa, Laura To: #Cornerstone Research < CornerstoneResearch@cornerstone.com > CC: #Information Resources < InformationResources@cornerstone.com > Hello there everyone, It looks like Compustat is back up and running (many many many thanks to Kevin Hunter!!!!!), but it has a new home (one that will have no other software installed on it that might conflict with it).  As a result, even if you used it before, you will have to follow the first-time user's instructions below. Things to Note: 1)  I believe we are still having a few default printer issues, so right now you will have to set your default to an SF printer (this should be fixed soon). 2)  It is also recommended that you make “Classic” (as reported data) the default database – otherwise you could inadvertently use “Compustat” figures (adjusted for mergers and acquisitions).  You can always choose to use the Compustat database for your data but it will be Classic data that will be accessed as the default. Instructions This only has to be done the first time you log in to Compustat.  After that, it should remember you and work just fine. First you will log in to Compustat's new terminal server: CRSFIRAPPS 1)  When you first log in: Execute the NewUser.reg program under Start | Programs | Research Insight. 2)  You must have a default printer selected before trying to search (you should only have to set this up once). If you are not sure how to set a default printer, contact #IT Help Desk. 3)  Lastly you need to tell Compustat where to find the files. Again, you only need to do this the first time you log in. If you do not do this, you will get an error message when you try to access the database. Here is what you do (it only takes about 5 minutes): After logging into the term sever, go to Start and select Research Insight Database Manager Under Database Areas, click on Properties Under Area 1 put: \\crsfir\ridata\na1 Under Area 2 put: \\crsfir\ridata\na2 Click Apply and then okay and exit the Manager Then go to start and click on Research Insight It will ask you to copy 596 (or some other large number) files to update, say okay and on the next screen click Copy It will start copying. This will take about 5 min. When it is done you should be ready to go. Good Luck, and let me know if you have any problems.  I apologize for all the downtime for this. -Laura Laura L. page_83.body_text: CLS Source CLS Group Holdings AG How to Cite the Source CLS Group Holdings AG Description CLS plays a fundamental role in the foreign exchange (FX) market – it operates the largest multicurrency cash settlement system to mitigate settlement risk for the FX transactions of its Members and their customers. Settlement of FX transactions requires the exchange of principal in two currencies. Settlement risk is the risk that one party pays the currency it sold but does not receive the currency it bought, resulting in a loss of principal. Background The impetus behind the creation of CLS came from regulatory concerns regarding the potential for FX settlement risk to be a major source of systemic risk, following the collapse of Bankhaus Herstatt. Launched in 2002 and owned by the world's leading FX banks, CLS settles payment instructions relating to underlying FX transactions in 18 currencies and certain other transactions that result in one-way payments in a subset of those currencies. How CLS Works CLS mitigates settlement risk through the provision of its unique payment versus payment settlement service which has direct links to the real time gross settlement (RTGS) systems of the currencies it settles. In addition to mitigating settlement risk, CLS also streamlines and standardizes FX operations, reducing costs. FX settlement includes potentially large cash funding values.  These values are materially reduced in CLS through the multilateral netting of the obligations between Member banks to deliver best in class liquidity management.  As regulatory requirements for larger liquidity buffers increase, the benefits from multilateral netting at an industry level are increasingly important. Time Period Covered ​ Access Contact CLS directly. Contact: London: +44 (0)207 971 5700 New York: +1 212 943 2290 Tokyo: +81 3 3517 2791 Hong Kong: +852 3520 6000 Cost Important Notes They do not currently offer a commercial product. They have a very high level monthly report on their website.  They mentioned that they are considering launching a commercial product but have no launch date or specifications available at this time.  They said that they can respond to requests for supplemental data from central banks working with them. They have no coverage of non-deliverable forwards.  They have coverage of a large range of OTC deliverable FX products. In the 18 currencies where they offer settlement ( https://www.cls-group.com/products/settlement/clssettlement/currencies/ ), they estimate that they have greater than 90% market share of the OTC FX market. AI Restrictions ​ AI Definitions/Capabilities ​ Updated 9/25/2025_aig

FX settlement includes potentially large cash funding values.  These values are materially reduced in CLS through the multilateral netting of the obligations between Member banks to deliver best in class liquidity management.  As regulatory requirements for larger liquidity buffers increase, the benefits from multilateral netting at an industry level are increasingly important.

In the 18 currencies where they offer settlement (https://www.cls-group.com/products/settlement/clssettlement/currencies/), they estimate that they have greater than 90% market share of the OTC FX market.

Errors in Thomson One Banker Hi Guys, Andrea and I have had a browser error lately where, 
after signing into One Banker, the company search box that usually appears in 
the upper left corner of the screen fails to materialize. The solution we've found is to clear your temporary 
internet files by clicking on Internet Options from the browser Tools menu.  
Once inside the "General" tab, click "Delete…", select Temporary Internet Files 
(you can keep everything else), and click "Delete.   Once your files are 
deleted,  close all browser windows and open your browser again.  TOB should 
work fine again.  I've noticed I've had to do this once a week or so lately, 
depending on usage. Hope this helps, Peter Gigante Information Specialist CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111-3685 415.229.8227 direct www.cornerstone.com

(10/9/2009) To: #Library < Library@cornerstone.com > E-TRACK was the system I

interest. http://iapps.courts.state.ny.us/webcivil/etrackFAQ An important thing to notice in NY state supreme 
court dockets: In many state and federal courts, a judge is assigned 
as soon as the case is filed.  New York takes a different approach.  Under the 
New York rules, a judge is not assigned to a case until one of the parties files 
a Request for Judicial Intervention (or "RJI") Form with the clerk.  Prior to 
the plaintiff filing an RJI, the court's only role is to issue an index number 
and be a repository for filed documents. This one page form triggers the court's 
actual entry into the case.  My guess would be that allowing cases to be filed 
without immediately involving the judges was to encourage out of court 
settlements, as there is a filing fee for the RJI. So what does this 
mean? WebCivil Supreme only displays cases for which a Request 
for Judicial Intervention (RJI) has been filed. You can manually add recently 
filed Supreme Court cases to your eTrack account and commence receiving 
notifications when an RJI is filed. Simply click on the "Add a Pre-RJI Case" 
link and enter the County, Index Number, Year of Filing and the Plaintiff and 
Defendant names.  You will not receive any email updates from eTrack unless and 
until an RJI is filed.  You can generally find the index number from the County 
Clerk's site: SCROLL http://iapps.courts.state.ny.us/iscroll/FNF913.htm I'll toss this on CRIKIT too.  It's free and public 
so why not. Peter Gigante Information Specialist CORNERSTONE RESEARCH 353 Sacramento Street, 23rd Floor San Francisco, CA  94111-3685 415.229.8227 direct 415.229.8199 fax www.cornerstone.com

CMA ABX on Datastream Available Indicies Some CMA ABX indices are available through Thomson Reuters' Datastream . For each index, the "Base Date" listed in Column F 
is the earliest date for which data is available. Available Data Types CDS Prem. Bid: Bid Rate – This shows the bid rate spread 
between the entity and the relevant benchmark curve. The rate is expressed in 
basis points. CDS Prem. Mid: Mid Rate – This shows the mid rate spread 
between the entity and the relevant benchmark curve. The rate is expressed in 
basis points. This is the default datatype. CDS Prem. Offered: Offer Rate – This shows the offer rate 
spread between the entity and the relevant benchmark curve. The rate is 
expressed in basis points. Veracity Score: Observed/Derived Indicator -   This shows 
the type of price used in calculating the bid and offer rate. The score is 
expressed numerical as 1 or 2. 1 is the numerical value for an observed market 
spread and 2 is for a derived spread. Cost The cost to retrieve ABX index data is $150 per index for all available 
history and all available data types.  There is no guarantee that all datapoints 
will be available for the entire timeseries of each index. Requesting data To request ABX index data, please send an email to #Information Resources indicating which indices you want to 
download.

Data product offerings can be reviewed in full at the following link: Market Data Products - CME Group . Important Notes You cannot produce the raw data . You may produce the derived output created from the data purchased.  You may provide information about what was purchased, but not the actual files used. If you think the client might want to share it with others, get in contact with Information Resources to figure out the best route to acquire the data.  It might involve the client purchasing the data directly with a license to share it with specific advisors. page_103.body_text: Competition Policy International (includes former GCP Magazine) Source Competition Policy International How to Cite the Source Competition Policy International Description Competition Policy International (CPI) is an independent knowledge-sharing organization focused on the diffusion of the most relevant antitrust information and content worldwide. CPI recognizes the importance of intellectually sound and balanced debates and aim to promote them across the world in the most innovative ways available. Created and managed by leaders in the competition policy community, CPI delivers timely commentary and analysis on antitrust and global competition policy matters through a variety of media and applications. CPI PUBLICATIONS CPI releases daily, weekly, and monthly antitrust-focused publications that reach several thousands of readers including enforcers, judges, lawyers, economists and academics in over 150 countries. CPI Columns are released regularly to provide up-to-date analysis on the most current antitrust issues. CPI also publishes books in hard-cover, paperback, and electronic formats. CPI Antitrust Chronicle (formerly known as GCP Magazine: The Online Magazine) The Antitrust Chronicle, our signature publication, is released bimonthly and consists of articles written by leading experts in competition law and economics. Articles focus on a specific topic at the forefront of competition law and policy debates.  CPI Antitrust Chronicle was formerly known as GCP Magazine: The Online Magazine and is dedicated to the intellectual integrity of all of the articles that it publishes. Articles and commentary published in the CPI journal and in CPI Antitrust Chronicle are selected and reviewed by editorial teams comprised of competition policy experts drawn from academia, authorities, courts, and law firms around the world. CPI Antitrust Chronicle has been published since November 2006. CPI Antitrust Chronicle does not solicit or accept payment for contributions, nor does it provide preference to any individual or entity that has purchased subscriptions to its publications. GCP does not accept funding from any entity, directly or indirectly, in exchange for publishing articles related to any case or ongoing controversy. CPI Journal CPI Journal was a peer-reviewed, academic journal that covers competition law, economics, and policy. Issues were published twice a year in the Spring and Autumn and in both print and online forms. The journal was published from 2005 to 2015. Issues were arranged thematically and included both new articles and 1 or 2 classic antitrust articles to refresh readers' memories of seminal discussions on important topics. Time Period Covered ​ Access Competition Policy International If you can't access something, try logging into this site: https://www.pymnts.com/cpi/account-management/ Another alternative:  If you see a blue box with a message on the web page that says "THIS ARTICLE IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR IP ADDRESS 4.30.144.108. Please verify email or join us to access premium content!" you can follow these steps: Click on "verify e-mail" Enter your e-mail address, you will then receive an e-mail with a link. Please save this e-mail with the link. Click on the link in the e-mail. Once this process has been finalized, you should now be able to access the Chronicles included in your CPI plan. If you use different browsers, you will need to verify each browser using the same link you received in your e-mail. This process only needs to be completed once. This link can also be used to verify a second device. Contact: #Information Resources Cost Free (Cornerstone has a subscription) Important Notes AI Restrictions Customer will not copy, reprint or distribute content except for in ways in accordance with this Agreement and as set forth in the Order. insider trading data that we retrieve either from Dialog or from ShareWorld (the

Calculation%20(cont’d) >> The 2nd and 3rd bullets on page 20

parser adjusts for splits.  The parser, which was written and modified over time 
several years ago (I believe it was written by Mike Tsai and may have been 
modified by various others including David Pedersen and Demetri Zaphiris and 
maybe others who I cannot identify), basically takes the text download from 
Dialog and turns it into an Excel spreadsheet.  The analysts then take that data 
and import it into the float template and manually adjust for splits if 
necessary. This is not the first time we've received incorrect 
information from the customer service representatives at Dialog as they are not

the questions we are asking of

Pharma Research - Patents on Biologics​ The pages from the 
Orange Book are on the LAN now. So after some more research, I 
think it’s going to be harder to come up with a definite answer than I 
originally thought. There has been a lot of discussion that: The new Biologics Act does not require any 
notice of relevant patents to the FDA, by the holders of patents on biological 
products licensed under the BCA, and it does not require that the FDA publish 
any listing of such patents. There is no Orange Book. Instead, the new Biologics 
Act creates a complex procedure for identification and litigation of potentially 
relevant patents, independent of any period of data exclusivity. The new 
Biologics Act allows the FDA to grant an application for approval of a 
biosimilar or interchangeable product without regard to the existence of any 
patent. So, we have to get 
creative. Here are some suggestions, in recommended order: 1) We could look into infringement 
litigation surrounding a particularly biologic and see what patents are 
asserted. 2) We could look at analogous patents in 
the EU. 3) We could search PTO’s records, though 
as I said before this might make some muddled waters. 4) We could try to pose the question to 
the companies directly (It’s a long shot but they may be able to give us a 
number without indicating the exact patents) Peter Gigante X8227 _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Wednesday, November 16, 2011 12:28 
PM To: Gigante, Peter Subject: RE: 
Pharma nonbillable question Hi 
Peter, Thanks for checking this out! 
Here’s a LAN folder for the pages: \\crbfs1\consulting\Pr actice 
Areas\Pharma\Biologics Research\Materials\Non-academic 
articles\Patents -heidi _____________________________________________ From: Gigante, Peter Sent: Wednesday, November 16, 2011 2:43 
PM To: Liu, Heidi Subject: RE: Pharma 
nonbillable question Hi 
Heidi, So it turns out 
that “always” was incorrect. Enbrel is the only biologic on your list that added 
the patent information to their prescribing information. For the small 
molecule drugs, we can look at Orange Book. Is there a LAN folder for the pages 
that I found? For the biologics, 
I’m trying some other tacks. Peter Gigante X8227 _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 6:20 
PM To: Gigante, Peter Subject: RE: 
Pharma nonbillable question Hi 
Peter, That sounds like a 
good idea. I checked Drugs@FDA and one of the drug websites really quickly – it 
looks like only prescription highlights are located there. Is there a database 
we could pull this from? Thanks so 
much! -heidi _____________________________________________ From: Gigante, Peter Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 8:45 
PM To: Liu, Heidi Subject: RE: Pharma 
nonbillable question Hi 
Heidi, So, patent searching in the 
USPTO website is not great. IP analytic databases like Innography are great for 
this, but we can’t afford them. One idea I had was looking at the “Full 
Prescribing Information” sheet that comes with all medications. They always list 
the patents covering the drug. For example, on the very last page of this Enbrel http://pi.amgen.com/united_states/enbrel/derm/enbrel_pi.pdf Patents 
covering methods, vectors, and/or host cells for making the product or methods 
for using the product: US Patent 
Nos. 7,915,225; 5,605,690; Re. 36,755. This would be 
readily available for all of the products you listed. Would that be 
sufficient? Searching the 
patent records would also be difficult since the patented process would not 
likely mention the name of the drug. For Enbrel, we could search for patents 
granted to Immunex dealing with TNF or dimeric protein or something else from 
the description, but it would be hard to tie that patent to Enbrel 
specifically. Peter Gigante X8227 _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 2:42 
PM To: Gigante, Peter Subject: RE: 
Pharma nonbillable question Our presentation 
is December 7 – if possible, sometime tomorrow would be great as we have a team 
meeting for this presentation. But whatever we can get before the deadline would 
be good – we’re just trying to establish the point that biologics on average 
have more patents. _____________________________________________ From: Gigante, Peter Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 5:39

nonbillable question Hi 
Heidi, No problem. I’ll 
see what I can find for you. Are you working with a particular 
deadline? Peter Gigante X8227 _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 2:38

PM To: Liu, Heidi Cc: #Information 
Resources Subject: RE: Pharma nonbillable 
question Heidi- We’ll get back to on 
this. -Andrea _____________________________________________ From: Liu, Heidi Sent: Tuesday, November 15, 2011 3:58 
PM To: #Information Resources Subject: Pharma nonbillable question Hello IR, I have two requests for a nonbillable: 1. I’m wondering about the 
pricing for the following reports that were found from a headline search: Biosimilars and Follow-On Biologics 
Report: The Global Outlook 2009-2024 Biosimilars (2009 - 2014) Biobetters – Major Players and Market 
Prospects Navigating the Biosimilars Market; The 
market landscape for biosimilars is in flux, with limited penetration now, but 
with the potential for growth for those who can navigate the market. Plus: A 
SWOT analysis of biosimilars by Anjan Selz. 2. Given a list of drugs, 
we are trying to figure out how many patents “cover” a list of particular 
biologic drugs. It looks like the patents on the FDA website are only for drugs 
that are small molecules. When we search the Patent and Trademark Office for the 
molecular name in the patent text and the drug company as the “assignee name” we 
come up with many hits. When we do the same thing to a list of small molecules 
we also get more hits than the number of patents on the FDA website. Is there a 
way to figure out which patents are directly relevant, or another database that 
has this? Please let me know if you have any questions. 
Thanks much! -heidi

page_119.body_text: CreditSights Source CreditSights How to Cite the Source Description Part of FitchSolutions, CreditSights provides comprehensive coverage of debt issuers and their securities across diverse market segments, including: Debt Issuance: Insights into global trends and investment-grade markets. Emerging Markets: Fundamental research on developing economies. High Yield: Analysis of high-yield securities from over 1,000 issuers. Asia Pacific: Macro and micro analysis of credits in the region. Special Situations: Research on debt in financial distress. Strategy: Analysis of macro trends in credit markets. U.S. Municipal: Insights on U.S. government entity credits. Credit ETFs: Research on bond-focused exchange-traded funds. Covenant Review is one of CreditSights' products. It covers 98% of all broadly syndicated loans, high yield bonds, investment grade, and private debt.  Extensive archive with over 5,000 bond/loan documents and analyses. Covenant Review covers every new issue of USD 250m+ in the market, providing analysis of the term sheet available within 24 hours after release, follow-up analysis on the draft credit agreement and updates on the final agreement. It has tools to compare covenants, analyze precedents, and understand trends. page_125.body_text: ​ UK/EU Soures for Case, Regulatory Proceedings and Arbitration General Litigation Bloomberg Law News Bloomberg Law has an excellent staff of journalists in the UK and EU and they often report on cases or arbitrations as they get filed.  We do not know how they find out since the courts are not public in any way, but they do find out.  They will often list the law firms and sometimes the attorneys involved.  Also if you contact them, they are generally responsive and will send you what they can.  Sometimes that is the complaint, and sometimes it is just more detail than they published in the article. We have the ability to search for litigation cases in the  UK two ways using Bloomberg:  News Alerts and Case Alerts.  Once you’ve identified a case that you’d like to track, we can set up a track and request documents as they become available.   You can set up a track on EU cases but the information  comes from CURIA (see below) and there is little information available. Very few ocuments are available for EU cases. CURIA - The Court of Justice for the European Union You can searh by court, case number or parties and by date. There is case information and a separate tab for documents. https://curia.europa.eu/jcms/jcms/j_6/en/ Lawtel (not currently subscribed) Lawtel is an online tool providing up to date case law, legislation and journal coverage. It also provides extensive coverage of EU law – both the ECJ and EU Commission are subscribers. We provide legally guaranteed primary law to practitioners working under the jurisdiction of UK, EU and International law.  Lawtel’s brochure is here: \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\Lawtel\Lawtel - Core Brochure.pdf The Pending Actions service from Lawtel enables users to search and track an action from when it has been acknowledged through to judgment, showing how proceedings develop leading up to hearing, meaning you will be the first to know about cases at the earliest possible stage. The service covers cases commenced in the Queen’s Bench Division (excluding the Administrative Court), the Commercial Court and Chancery Division (excluding the Bankruptcy Court) from January 2010. The database will inform users of the main issues pertaining to the case along with the case progress and final judgment. Once proceedings have been commenced and a Claim Form has been filed, we will add basic information relating to the case (Party names, Court, Case number, Date filed). For selected cases, once (and if) the Particulars of Claim is available, we will add additional information, such as subjects, keywords, a summary of the case and legal representation (if available). Example pending action \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\Lawtel\Example Pending Action from Lawtel - Banking and Finance 6-2015.rtf IR Notes:  Generally a few weeks behind Bloomberg. Competition/Antitrust MLEX Mlex is an antitrust news and case and regulation tracking service called MLex, specifically the module MLex EU within this service.  MLex EU tracks antitrust litigation in the EU and UK and publishes articles and commentary on the litigation both as the case is developing and after it is over.  They also follow and publish articles about regulations and potential regulations pertaining to antitrust issues.  You can set up alerts for types of cases, courts, industries, etc. as well as save searches that you do. PaRR PaRR is a daily, global news service devoted to antitrust/competition law. Our global team of investigative journalists report on all aspects of antitrust/competition law including merger review, enforcement actions, intellectual property and litigations. PaRR's team of reporters, analysts and translators are based around the world in Asia, Europe and the Americas. In addition to our news offerings, subscribers also have access to our Global Case Database and M&A Timetable. The Global Case Database contains competition cases from 2010-present from Europe, the US, Brazil, India and China. The M&A Timetable contains merger review filing timetable information for deals between large, publicly traded companies over the past ten years. GCR GCR provides online competition news that can be delivered to you daily if you wish.  This includes: facts on significant deals and developments, promotions and departures, news and analysis on competition enforcement agencies, a searchable archive comprising thousands of stories published since December 1997. If you are interested in accessing this publication, simply go to: http://www.globalcompetitionreview.com and use our Username: corner and Password: stone to log in.  If you would like to start receiving the daily email you can go here: http://www.globalcompetitionreview.com/briefing/ and enter your email. European Commission Competition Cases Source of EC Competition Case Decisions - covers Antitrust, Cartel, Merger and State Aid Cases:- Link to Search page. Law360: International Trade (section) The international trade section covers litigation, regulation and legislation related to exports and imports. The section tracks trade and tariff disputes, customs controls and policy developments, with a focus on proceedings at the Court of International Trade, the International Trade Commission and the World Trade Organization.  To access: https://www.law360.com/internationaltrade . International Arbitration TDM OGEMID’s Transnational Dispute Management (TDM) journal.  “TDM is a peer-review online journal publishing about various aspects of international arbitration with a special focus on investment arbitration. Since the first issue was published in 2004 it has gained popularity among a large number of law firms, academics and other professionals in the field of arbitration.”  Included is automatic membership to OGEMIND.  You can find out more about the organization and TDM here: http://www.transnational-dispute-management.com/ogemid/ . You can view material ahead of its appearance in a regular structured issues of the Journal by going to the “Advance Publication” tab on the home page.  You can also sign up for alerts and monitor the RSS feed for advance publication http://www.transnational-dispute-management.com/rss/advance.xml . Here is a email alert of Advance Publications from TDM: \\CRNYFS2\Admin\London Working Group\IR Resources\TDM update alert.msg GAR GAR reports on arbitration cases, deals and community news in the United States, North America and globally. The benefits of a Premium GAR subscription are: Keep up to date Deal and case news : Legal and policy developments Community news : Departures, promotions and mergers Understand the market Surveys, league tables and country profiles High-profile interviews, commentary , and roundtable discussions Strategy and firm management In-depth reporting from GAR Live and other arbitration community events Identify your competitors GAR100 : A guide to the world's leading arbitration practices Know your arbitration centre The Guide to Regional Arbitration: ‘Whitelists’ and directories of arbitral providers nested in particular regions, explaining which are already worth using and which are ones to watch Strengthen your knowledge Special reports : Insight submitted by experts from leading firms worldwide, with a focus on the hot topics of the moment GAR Know-How : An interactive resource providing quick-and-easy comparisons of current arbitration process and procedure across multiple jurisdictions Get the background story Access to the archive covering over 8 years of historical news and analysis Law360: International Arbitration (search only) There is not a specific section on this, however it does exist as a practice area in the advanced search feature.  Thus we can create a search that provides the type of articles we want and then set it as an alert so that it will push out a “newsletter” to whoever wants to see it.

PaRR

PaRR is a daily, global news service devoted to antitrust/competition law. recognise the "Q."  Simply remove the Q from the ticker when extracting data 
from CRSP.

Time Period Covered Access Information Resources staff only.  IR only **SF** Contact: Tel: 020 7400 3171 Email: cs@cla.co.uk Cost $0 Important Notes We have copyright coverage for UK and international resources for our UK employees through CLA.   You can check whether we have permission through the link below.  See this Brochure for more information. What you can copy Most major UK and international publications are covered, but you can use our Check Permissions search tool on the CLA website to make sure. How much you can copy You can copy up to one chapter, one article, or 5% of a publication, whichever is greater. These copying limits mean you can use the content you want in a flexible way, while remaining certain that you're covered.
